headline: Identification is becoming law: DRS barcodes, construction product QR labels and GB UDI all move closer
executive_summary: Across all three sectors this week's picture is consistent: regulators and scheme operators are writing unique identifiers, scannable data carriers and digital product records into binding requirements. In retail, Exchange for Change has confirmed that every in-scope drinks container will need a newly registered barcode before the October 2027 DRS launch, and the EU's DPP Registry and EUDR deadlines bear on UK exporters. In construction, MHCLG's White Paper and GSR consultation propose unique identifiers and QR-code labels on all construction products with regulations due by end-2026. In healthcare, MHRA's draft 2026 regulations would make UDI compulsory in Great Britain from mid-2027. For GS1 UK the priorities are to influence how 'unique identifier' and 'data carrier' are defined in each instrument, and to get members allocating GTINs and cleaning product master data now rather than in 2027.
cross_sector_themes: Regulators are converging on 'unique identifier + scannable data carrier + digital record' as the traceability pattern
QR codes powered by GS1 can serve POS, DRS, DPP, construction labelling and UDI from a single symbol
2027 is the crunch year: DRS go-live, GB UDI entry into force, construction GSR commencement, first EU DPP obligations
Master data quality (GTIN, GLN, attributes) is the common readiness gap across sectors

sector_overviews.headline: DRS moves into its final year; EU digital product data rules keep tightening for UK exporters
sector_overviews.summary: The dominant retail signal is the deposit return scheme: with Exchange for Change confirming fees, readiness tracking and mandatory barcode changes, the 1 October 2026 countdown turns GTIN re-allocation into a board-level programme for drinks producers and own-label retailers. In parallel, the EU DPP Registry going live and EUDR's 30 December 2026 application date mean UK exporters need registry-ready identifiers and location-level traceability. The 2029 e-invoicing mandate is further out but reinforces the same master-data discipline.
top_priorities: UK Deposit Return Scheme: one-year countdown starts 1 October 2026 – producer fees announced, barcodes must change
European Commission launches the Digital Product Passport Registry – batteries first from 18 February 2027
EU Deforestation Regulation applies from 30 December 2026
watchlist: Packaging EPR labelling obligations and fee modulation

sector_overviews.headline: Unique identifiers and QR data carriers are now written into the government's construction products plan
sector_overviews.summary: The Construction Products Reform White Paper and the General Safety Requirement consultation together define a regime in which every construction product must be uniquely identified and carry a digital label linking to a digital product record, enforced by OPSS with the Building Safety Regulator. With regulations targeted for end-2026 and commencement in late 2027, this is the window for GS1 UK to shape identifier definitions and for manufacturers to allocate GTINs and build product data.

sector_overviews.headline: Statutory UDI for Great Britain is on the horizon while Scan4Safety scales nationally
sector_overviews.summary: MHRA's draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026 would make UDI compulsory for GB, with adoption planned for December 2026 and entry into force in June 2027. This turns the NHS's GS1-based Scan4Safety and MDOR practice into a legal requirement for all manufacturers. NHS Supply Chain's IMS programme and the New Hospitals Programme's 2027 GS1 requirement give trusts the infrastructure to use that data at the point of care.
top_priorities: MHRA draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026: UDI to become compulsory for devices placed on the GB market
NHS Scan4Safety: New Hospitals Programme requires GS1 standards from 2027; NHS Supply Chain IMS roll-out to 2031

items.title: MHRA draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026: UDI to become compulsory for devices placed on the GB market
items.issuing_body: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
items.summary: MHRA has notified the WTO of draft pre-market regulations for medical devices and IVDs in Great Britain. They make Unique Device Identification compulsory (Basic UDI-DI, UDI-DI and UDI-PI), require implant cards, introduce an international reliance route and align classification with IMDRF. Adoption is planned for December 2026 with entry into force in June 2027 and three- to five-year transitions.
items.what_changed: On 8 May 2026 MHRA published the draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026 on the WTO notification portal, with a UK impact survey open until 19 June 2026. Manufacturers would need to assign a UDI before placing a device on the GB market, carry it on the device and packaging, and include it in registration records and technical documentation. Healthcare organisations implanting devices must give patients implant cards. The rules complement the post-market surveillance requirements already in force since 16 June 2025. Transitional periods of three years (general devices) and five years (IVDs) are proposed; the reliance pathway is expected in 2028.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: GS1 is an accredited UDI issuing agency internationally and more than 95 per cent of devices used in the NHS already carry GS1 GTINs as their UDI-DI, with GS1 DataMatrix as the preferred carrier and GMN as the Basic UDI-DI. A statutory GB UDI requirement converts what has been NHS procurement policy (Scan4Safety, MDOR) into law for every manufacturer selling into GB, driving GS1 UK membership and Numberbank usage among MedTech companies and reinforcing the GTIN/GLN/GSRN model in trusts. Key watch-points for GS1 UK: that MHRA designates issuing entities compatible with GS1 (as the EU and FDA do), that the GB UDI database schema aligns with GDSN/GUDID attributes, and that implant-card requirements reference the UDI in scannable form. Members with EU MDR UDI already in place will largely reuse it; UK-only manufacturers and NHS trusts' IMS/EPR systems need to prepare.
affected_stakeholders: Medical device and IVD manufacturers and UK Responsible Persons
NHS trusts and Scan4Safety / MDOR programmes

key_dates.label: WTO notification and draft published

items.title: UK Deposit Return Scheme: one-year countdown starts 1 October 2026 – producer fees announced, barcodes must change
items.issuing_body: Exchange for Change (Deposit Management Organisation) / Defra
items.summary: Exchange for Change, the appointed Deposit Management Organisation for England, Northern Ireland and Scotland, has published its intended producer fees and new retailer-readiness measures ahead of the DRS go-live on 1 October 2027. It has confirmed that every in-scope drinks container must carry a barcode registered on the Scheme Article List and that existing barcodes – including international ones – will need to change.
items.what_changed: The UK-wide deposit return scheme for single-use PET, aluminium and steel drinks containers launches on 1 October 2027 under The Deposit Scheme for Drinks Containers (England and Northern Ireland) Regulations 2025, with parallel Scottish legislation and a compatible Welsh scheme that also covers glass. On 1 October 2026 the formal one-year countdown begins. Exchange for Change has announced intended producer fees, introduced measures to track retailer readiness, and updated its material specification: containers must display a unique barcode (EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A or UPC-E) that complies with the GS1 General Specifications, is registered on the Scheme Article List and is readable by reverse vending machines and counting centres. Each container within a multipack needs its own barcode, distinct from the outer pack. Producers must register, apply the deposit, report volumes and meet scheme labelling requirements; retailers must charge deposits, host return points and refund consumers.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: This is the single largest forced re-identification event UK grocery has faced: the scheme operator has stated that all existing product barcodes on in-scope containers will need to change and be registered, which means new GTIN allocation for thousands of SKUs across GS1 UK's drinks-producer, brand-owner and retailer members. The specification explicitly requires compliance with the GS1 General Specifications, placing GS1 UK's GTIN Management Standard, barcode quality guidance and My Numberbank at the centre of member readiness. It also creates a natural on-ramp for QR codes powered by GS1 (GS1 Digital Link), since RVMs will read both linear and 2D symbols and a single code can serve POS, DRS, consumer information and future DPP/EUDR needs. Risks: members who leave GTIN and artwork changes to 2027 will collide with retailer listing windows, RVM certification and stock run-down; poorly allocated GTINs (reused numbers, shared multipack/unit codes) will cause refund failures and reconciliation disputes. GS1 UK is not the scheme administrator – scope, fees and registration questions belong to Exchange for Change – but identification quality is squarely GS1 UK's remit.
gs1_standards_implicated: GS1 Digital Link (QR codes powered by GS1)

items.title: MHCLG General Safety Requirement for construction products: unique identifiers and QR-code data carriers proposed for all products
items.issuing_body: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
items.summary: Government is consulting on a General Safety Requirement (GSR) for currently unregulated construction products using Schedule 11 of the Building Safety Act 2022. Manufacturers would have to label products with their name, address, a unique product identifier and a data carrier such as a QR code linking to digital product information, to enable traceability and recalls.
items.what_changed: Published alongside the Construction Products Reform White Paper on 25 February 2026 and closing 20 May 2026, the consultation proposes that all construction products placed on the UK market be safe, with duties on manufacturers, importers and distributors and enforcement powers for the national regulator for construction products (OPSS) with Local Authority Trading Standards. Paragraph 7.17–7.18 require labelling with a unique identifier and a data carrier (e.g. QR code) affixed to the product or, where impossible, its packaging or product information. Government welcomes PAS 2000:2026 as a code of practice. Regulations are targeted for introduction by end-2026 with commencement in late 2027.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: This is the clearest UK regulatory signal yet that construction products will need a globally unique identifier plus a scannable digital label – the GTIN carried in a QR code powered by GS1 (GS1 Digital Link) is the established, cross-sector way to do this and is already on many products that overlap with retail. GS1 UK responded to the 2025 CPR paper advocating exactly this model and its interoperability with CCPI. For GS1 UK the opportunity is to be named or referenced in the final regulations and guidance as an acceptable identifier scheme, and to grow membership among construction manufacturers who have never barcoded. The risk is fragmentation: proprietary or scheme-specific identifiers (e.g. UPIN-only approaches) would break the 'golden thread' across merchants, contractors and building owners. Members who wait for the SI will have under a year to allocate GTINs, build product data records and change labelling.

GS1 Digital Product Passport provisional standard
affected_stakeholders: OPSS / national regulator for construction products

items.title: Construction Products Reform White Paper: digital product information by default, database of products and digital product records
items.summary: The White Paper sets the direction for a new construction products regime: information must be available digitally for all products, labelling must include unique product identifiers linked to up-to-date information through a digital label such as a QR code, and government will establish a construction products database and digital product records, staying aligned with EU DPP where appropriate.
items.what_changed: Building on the Building Safety Act 2022 and the Grenfell Inquiry recommendations, the White Paper commits to: a general safety requirement, a strengthened national regulator, reformed conformity assessment, a database of construction products, digital product records accessible via QR code, and digital standards developed with industry to promote consistency of product information. It notes the Construction Products (Amendment) Regulations 2025 came into force on 8 January 2026 to continue recognising products conforming to the EU CPR.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: The paper's language – 'unique product identifiers', 'digital label (such as a QR code)', 'interoperable, accessible and enduring' information – mirrors GS1's identify/capture/share model. A government product database keyed on identifiers is a strong use case for GTIN as the primary key and GLN for manufacturers, and the commitment to develop digital standards with industry is the window for GS1 UK to embed GS1 Digital Link, GDSN attributes and the GS1 DPP standard alongside CCPI and LEXiCON templates. GS1 UK's existing DPP-readiness work with construction members is directly transferable.
gs1_standards_implicated: GS1 Digital Product Passport provisional standard

items.title: European Commission launches the Digital Product Passport Registry – batteries first from 18 February 2027
items.summary: The EU Digital Product Passport Registry – the central index of DPP unique identifiers and metadata under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation – is live, with a testing environment open. Batteries become the first mandatory category on 18 February 2027, with textiles, construction products, electronics, iron and steel expected to follow.
items.what_changed: The Commission has launched the DPP Registry as the European indexing service for Digital Product Passports. It stores unique identifiers, registration data and key metadata while detailed product data stays with the business or its DPP service provider. Economic operators remain responsible for data accuracy and availability and must lodge a backup copy with a DPP service provider for in-scope products. The first binding requirements apply to certain batteries from 18 February 2027 under the Batteries Regulation.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: DPPs are built on exactly the three pillars GS1 UK licenses and standardises: a globally unique product identifier (GTIN, serialised where required), a data carrier (QR code / Data Matrix using GS1 Digital Link) and interoperable data sharing (GS1 Web Vocabulary, EPCIS, the GS1 DPP provisional standard). UK manufacturers exporting batteries, textiles, construction products or electronics to the EU will need registry-ready identifiers within 18 months. For GS1 UK this validates the 'one QR code for POS, DRS, DPP and consumer information' narrative and creates demand for productDNA / GDSN attribute readiness and GS1 Digital Link resolver services. The UK Construction Products Reform White Paper also commits to staying aligned with EU DPP plans, so this is a leading indicator for domestic requirements. Note: the Registry does not itself mandate GS1 identifiers; ESPR delegated acts define acceptable identifier schemes, and GS1 is working through CEN/CENELEC JTC 24 to have GS1 keys recognised.
gs1_standards_implicated: GS1 Digital Product Passport provisional standard
affected_stakeholders: UK exporters of batteries, textiles, construction products, electronics, iron and steel

items.title: NHS Scan4Safety: New Hospitals Programme requires GS1 standards from 2027; NHS Supply Chain IMS roll-out to 2031
items.summary: NHS England's Scan4Safety pages confirm the policy drivers now underpinning point-of-care scanning: mandatory MDOR submissions, the 10-Year Health Plan, the DHSC MedTech Strategy, and the New Hospitals Programme's requirement for GS1 standards adoption in all hospitals delivered from 2027, supported by NHS Supply Chain's Inventory Management Systems programme running to 2031.
items.what_changed: Scan4Safety is being scaled from demonstrator sites to a national capability. NHS Supply Chain, with NHS England investment, is providing trusts with IMS infrastructure, scanners and deployment support through 2031; the National Patient Safety Team holds the mandate; MDOR receives high-risk device data; and NHS Commercial has set Scan4Safety as a strategic priority. Scotland and Wales fund national programmes and Northern Ireland uses GS1 standards for asset identification within Encompass/EPIC.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: This is GS1 UK's flagship healthcare programme: every person (GSRN on wristbands per DCB1077), product (GTIN with GS1 DataMatrix) and place (GLN via Location Manager) is identified with GS1 keys, and NHS England centrally funds trust membership. The New Hospitals Programme requirement makes GS1 adoption a design input for new estates. The GS1 UK survey finding that missing or unscannable barcodes on medicines packaging disrupt pharmacy workflows points to a gap GS1 UK should pursue with MHRA and manufacturers.

items.title: EU Deforestation Regulation applies from 30 December 2026 – due diligence statements needed for in-scope UK exports
items.summary: From 30 December 2026 operators placing cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber, soya, wood and derived products on the EU market or exporting them must prove they are deforestation-free and legally produced, supported by a due diligence statement with geolocation data.
items.what_changed: EUDR moves from policy to implementation on 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators. Businesses must collect geolocation of production plots, assess and mitigate risk, and submit due diligence statements through the EU Information System, with reference numbers travelling with the goods. UK producers, traders and retailers supplying the EU – including GB to Northern Ireland movements – are in scope.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: EUDR does not mandate any particular standard, but compliance at scale depends on consistently identifying products (GTIN), trading partners and locations (GLN for plots, sites and legal entities) and recording custody events (EPCIS 2.0) so due diligence statement references can be linked to specific consignments. GS1 UK's role is to position GLN and EPCIS as the interoperable backbone for members' traceability solutions and to keep members clear that GS1 standards support but do not constitute compliance.

items.title: UK e-invoicing mandate: structured e-invoices for VAT-registered B2B/B2G from 1 April 2029 – roadmap due at Budget 2026
items.summary: Government has confirmed that from 1 April 2029 VAT-registered businesses must issue structured e-invoices for B2B and B2G transactions, with technical standards and transitional arrangements to be set out in an implementation roadmap at Budget 2026.
items.what_changed: Following the 2025 consultation, the mandate is confirmed in principle with co-design through 2026, a full roadmap at Budget 2026, preparation in 2027–28 and go-live on 1 April 2029. Whether roll-out is phased or a single switch-on is still to be confirmed.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1: Structured e-invoices need unambiguous party, location and product identifiers: GLNs for buyer/seller/ship-to and GTINs for line items are already used in GS1 EANCOM/EDI and PEPPOL BIS in the NHS. GS1 UK should make sure the roadmap's technical standards (likely PEPPOL/UBL-based) permit GS1 identifiers and should treat 2027–28 as a master-data clean-up window for members across all three sectors.
